fi-corydoras-panda.title: Panda Cory
fi-corydoras-panda.sci: Corydoras panda (now often listed as Hoplisoma panda)
fi-corydoras-panda.summary: A small, peaceful bottom-dweller with panda-like black patches. Happiest in a group and in slightly cool water.
rows: 18 × 12 in footprint (about 11 gal) or larger for a small group
Keep at least 6 together. They're shy and inactive alone
Omnivore. Sinking pellets or wafers as the staple, plus live or frozen daphnia, brine shrimp and bloodworm
72–77°F (22–25°C). Long-term warmer water shortens its life
Easy, but sensitive to dirty water and dirty substrate
Upper Amazon, Peru. Nearly all in the trade are farm-raised
notes: Use soft sand or smooth gravel and keep it clean. Corys can lose their whiskers (barbels) over dirty or rough substrate.
Avoid undergravel filters. Don't keep with large or aggressive fish.
warn: Likes cooler water (72–77°F). That doesn't overlap with heat-lovers like German blue rams (81–86°F).
